questions.stem: Phenol reacts with bromine water to give a white precipitate of
questions.explanation: The -OH group strongly activates the ring towards electrophilic substitution at the ortho and para positions. In aqueous bromine all three positions react, giving a white precipitate of 2,4,6-tribromophenol. Monobromophenols form in a non-polar solvent such as CS$_2$ at low temperature.

optionRationale.1: 2-Bromophenol is formed in a non-polar solvent at low temperature, not in bromine water.
optionRationale.2: 4-Bromophenol is formed in a non-polar solvent at low temperature, not in bromine water.
optionRationale.3: The -OH group is retained in the product.

questions.stem: In the fermentation of glucose to ethanol, the enzyme that converts glucose into ethanol and carbon dioxide is
questions.explanation: Invertase converts sucrose into glucose and fructose, and zymase, present in yeast, then converts glucose and fructose into ethanol and carbon dioxide. Diastase converts starch to maltose, and maltase converts maltose to glucose.

optionRationale.2: Invertase acts on sucrose, not glucose.
optionRationale.3: Diastase acts on starch to give maltose.
optionRationale.4: Maltase acts on maltose to give glucose.

questions.objective: Recall the enzymes in ethanol fermentation

questions.stem: How many moles of hydrogen gas are liberated when 1 mol of glycerol (propane-1,2,3-triol) reacts with excess sodium?
questions.explanation: Glycerol has three -OH groups. Each -OH reacts as R-OH + Na $\rightarrow$ R-ONa + 1/2 H$_2$, so three hydroxyl groups release 3 x 1/2 = 1.5 mol of H$_2$.

optionRationale.1: Three moles would count one mole of H$_2$ per -OH group instead of half a mole.
optionRationale.3: One mole corresponds to a diol, not a triol.
optionRationale.4: A half mole corresponds to a monohydric alcohol.

questions.objective: Count hydrogen evolved from polyhydric alcohols

questions.stem: Phenol is heated with chloroform and aqueous sodium hydroxide, and the product is acidified. The main product is
questions.explanation: This is the Reimer-Tiemann reaction. Dichlorocarbene, generated from chloroform and base, attacks the phenoxide ring at the ortho position. Hydrolysis of the dichloromethyl group gives a -CHO group, so the product is 2-hydroxybenzaldehyde (salicylaldehyde).

optionRationale.1: Salicylic acid is obtained in the Kolbe-Schmidt reaction using CO$_2$.
optionRationale.4: The main product has the -CHO group at the ortho position and not a -COOH at para.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the most acidic?
questions.explanation: The -NO$_2$ group is electron withdrawing and stabilises the phenoxide ion by dispersing the negative charge, so 4-nitrophenol is a stronger acid than phenol. The electron releasing -CH$_3$ group in 4-methylphenol destabilises the phenoxide. Cyclohexanol has no resonance stabilisation.

optionRationale.1: Phenol is less acidic than the nitro substituted phenol.
optionRationale.2: The methyl group is electron releasing and decreases acidity.
optionRationale.3: Cyclohexanol is an alcohol, with an alkoxide that has no resonance stabilisation.

questions.stem: The total number of structural isomers (alcohols and ethers, ignoring stereoisomers) with the molecular formula C$_4$H$_{10}$O is
questions.explanation: There are four alcohols: butan-1-ol, butan-2-ol, 2-methylpropan-1-ol and 2-methylpropan-2-ol. There are three ethers: methoxypropane, 2-methoxypropane and ethoxyethane. The total number of structural isomers is therefore 4 + 3 = 7, and stereoisomers of butan-2-ol are not counted separately here.

optionRationale.3: Five misses two of the three ethers.
optionRationale.4: Eight would include a non-existent isomer, such as a repeated ether.

questions.stem: Methoxyethane reacts with one mole of HI at 373 K. The major products are
questions.explanation: The ether oxygen is first protonated. The iodide ion then attacks the less hindered, smaller alkyl group by an S$_N$2 path, giving CH$_3$I and leaving the larger group as the alcohol, C$_2$H$_5$OH. Excess HI would convert the alcohol to the iodide.

optionRationale.1: This reverses the rule; the halide attacks the smaller alkyl group in S$_N$2 cleavage.
optionRationale.3: Both alkyl iodides form only with excess HI.
optionRationale.4: HI supplies iodide, so some alkyl iodide must be formed.

questions.objective: Predict the products of cleavage of an unsymmetrical ether

questions.stem:
Assertion (A): 2-Nitrophenol is steam volatile, whereas 4-nitrophenol is not.
Reason (R): 2-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, whereas 4-nitrophenol has intermolecular hydrogen bonding.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: In 2-nitrophenol the -OH hydrogen bonds to the neighbouring -NO$_2$ group inside the same molecule, so the molecules do not associate and the compound is more volatile. In 4-nitrophenol the hydrogen bonding is between molecules, giving association and low volatility. The reason correctly explains the assertion.

optionRationale.2: The reason is a correct explanation of the assertion, so it is not merely a true statement.
optionRationale.3: The assertion is true: 2-nitrophenol is steam volatile.
optionRationale.4: The reason is true: the hydrogen bonding in 2-nitrophenol is intramolecular.

questions.objective: Relate hydrogen bonding type to steam volatility

questions.stem: Match the compound in List-I with its class or source in List-II.
questions.explanation: Ethylene glycol has two -OH groups, so it is dihydric (A-II). Glycerol has three, so it is trihydric (B-I). Phenol has -OH on a benzene ring (C-III). Methanol is made industrially from water gas, CO + 2H$_2$, over a ZnO-Cr$_2$O$_3$ catalyst (D-IV).

optionRationale.1: This code interchanges the matches of A and B; the correct pairs are A-II and B-I.
optionRationale.2: This code interchanges the matches of C and D; the correct pairs are C-III and D-IV.
optionRationale.4: This code interchanges the matches of A and C; the correct pairs are A-II and C-III.

questions.objective: Classify alcohols and recall the manufacture of methanol

right: III. Hydroxy compound with -OH on a benzene ring
IV. Obtained commercially by hydrogenation of carbon monoxide

questions.stem:
Consider the following statements about phenol.
A. Phenol gives a violet colour with neutral ferric chloride.
B. Oxidation of phenol with chromic acid gives benzoquinone.
C. Phenol is a weaker acid than ethanoic acid.
D. The -OH group of phenol directs an incoming electrophile to the meta position.
Which statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Phenol gives a violet complex with ferric chloride, is oxidised to benzoquinone by chromic acid, and is weaker than carboxylic acids ($pK_a$ about 10 against 4.76). The -OH group activates the ring and directs to the ortho and para positions, so D is wrong.

optionRationale.1: D is wrong because -OH is ortho and para directing, and C is also correct.
optionRationale.2: D is wrong, and A is also correct.
optionRationale.3: It includes the wrong statement D and omits the correct statements A and C.
